en.title: Dividing Single Consonants in Romanian
en.summary: When a single consonant stands between two vowels, it always moves to the second syllable.

sections.title: The Basic Rule
paragraphs: Romanian syllables follow clear and simple patterns. When one consonant sits between two vowels, it always joins the second vowel. This means the first syllable ends with an open vowel sound. Linguists call this an open syllable. The rule works everywhere in Romanian, whether at the start, middle, or end of words. Learning this rule helps you read new words smoothly. It also makes your rhythm sound natural.

sections.title: Mouth and Voice Flow
paragraphs: Keep your voice flowing smoothly between the sounds. Do not stop your airflow at the end of the first vowel. Let the vowel ring clearly before your mouth prepares the consonant. For example, your lips should close for the consonant only when starting the next beat. The vocal stress usually falls on the first part of common words. Say the stressed syllable with a slightly higher pitch, then drop your voice gently on the second beat.

sections.title: The Word Ma-mă
paragraphs: A classic example of this pattern is the word **ma-mă** /ˈma.mə/, which means mother. The letter **m** sits between the vowels **a** and **ă**. Following our rule, that middle consonant belongs entirely to the second syllable. You say **ma**, then you say **mă**. Stress the first syllable firmly. Your mouth opens wide for the first vowel, then your lips tap together to start the second syllable cleanly.

sections.title: Mistakes to Avoid
paragraphs: English speakers often pull the middle consonant backward into the first syllable. They might try to say *mam-uh*. That changes the natural rhythm of Romanian. Avoid closing your lips too early while saying the first vowel. Keep the first vowel open and pure. Give the consonant completely to the second syllable, and keep the final vowel short and relaxed.
